name: M1
description: Haplogroup M1 is a remarkable subclade of M that undertook a back-migration from Asia into Northeast Africa and the Near East, making it the only M-derived lineage found at significant frequencies in Africa. M1 is most common in Ethiopia (~20%), Somalia (~15%), Egypt (~10%), and among Berber populations of North Africa (~10%). Unlike other M subclades which predominantly mark South and East Asian lineages, M1 appears to represent an ancient re-migration from southwestern Asia (possibly the Arabian Peninsula or the Levant) back into Africa via the Horn of Africa, reversing part of the Out-of-Africa trajectory.
interestingFact: M1 is sometimes called the 'return migrant' haplogroup — it is a branch of M, which itself originated in Asia from the Out-of-Africa migration, but M1 subsequently migrated back into Africa from the Near East. This reversal, detectable in the mtDNA, provides direct genetic evidence that prehistoric humans moved not just out of Africa but also back into it — a 'southern route back-migration' that brought Asian-derived mtDNA to the Horn of Africa tens of thousands of years ago.

statistics.modernFrequency: ~1% globally; higher in Northeast Africa and Near East
